subject: MATHEMATICS FOR ELECTRICAL SCIENCE AND PHYSICAL SCIENCE – 2

details.name: MATHEMATICS FOR ELECTRICAL SCIENCE AND PHYSICAL SCIENCE – 2
details.prerequisites:
Basic knowledge in    
single variable 
calculus.

topics:
Partial derivatives of 
functions with two variables

Partial derivatives viewed as rate of 
change and slope3s

Partial derivatives of functions with more than 
two variables

Maxima and 
minima of functions of two variables - relative maxima and 
minima

Reversing the order of integration in double 
integrals

change of coordinates in double integrals (Cartesian to 
polar)

Triple
integral in Cartesian and cylindrical coordinates.

Vector valued function of single variable - derivative of vector 
valued function
Concept of scalar and vector fields

Green’s theorem (for simply connected domains, without proof) 
and applications to evaluating line integrals

Surface integrals over surfaces of the form 
z=g(x, y)
Flux integrals over surfaces of the form z = g(x, y)

Using Divergence theorem 
to find flux

partA.description:
2 Questions from 
each module.  
Total of 8 Questions, 
each carrying 3 marks

partB.description:
Each question carries 9 marks.  
Two questions will be given from each 
module, out of which 1 question should be 
answered.  
Each question can have a maximum of 3 
sub divisions.

courseOutcomes.description:
Compute the partial and total derivatives and maxima and 
minima of multivariable functions and to apply in engineering 
problems.

Understand theoretical idea of multiple integrals and to apply 
them to find areas and volumes of geometrical shapes.

Compute the derivatives and line integrals of vector functions 
and to learn their applications.

Apply the concepts of surface and volume integrals and to 
learn their inter-relations and applications.
